root_cause.text: The UFS suspend path for RPM level zero (device and link active) did not flush the exception event handling work (eeh_work), allowing a pending work to access the host controller after the system had entered a deep power-down state.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `flush_work(&hba->eeh_work)` and `ufshcd_disable_auto_bkops(hba)` inside the condition `if (req_dev_pwr_mode == UFS_ACTIVE_PWR_MODE && req_link_state == UIC_LINK_ACTIVE_STATE)`, which corresponds to RPM level zero. The commit message explicitly states this bypass created a race condition leading to illegal hardware access and system crash.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing disable of auto-bkops and flush of eeh work when suspending with device already in active mode.
intent_record.what: Added calls to ufshcd_disable_auto_bkops(hba) and flush_work(&hba->eeh_work) inside the if block that checks for UFS_ACTIVE_PWR_MODE and UIC_LINK_ACTIVE_STATE before jumping to vops_suspend.
intent_record.how: This ensures that when the device and link are already active during suspend, background operations are disabled and any pending exception event work is flushed before proceeding with the vendor-specific suspend path.

grouping_result.intent: Fix missing disable of auto-bkops and flush of eeh work when suspending with device already in active mode.

relevance_review.reason: The group's core intent directly addresses the vulnerability root cause by fixing the missing flush of eeh work during suspend when the device is already in active mode.
